cards.explanation: The answer is the promised eternal inheritance. Christ is the mediator of a new covenant so that those who are called may receive it. He has died to redeem them, and that's how it comes to them. An inheritance is something handed to you, friends, not something you earn by working a double shift.

The word is first. Christ died to redeem the called from the transgressions committed under the first covenant (Hebrews 9:15). So His death reaches back to the transgressions from the first covenant. First is the word that fits, friends.

A will takes effect when the one who made it has died. A will does not take effect until then, and it cannot be executed while he is still alive (Hebrews 9:17). Nobody gets to cash in an inheritance while the person is still at the table eating cookies. The writer uses that everyday fact to explain why a death matters for the new covenant.

The word is blood. Since a will needs a death, the first covenant was not put into effect without blood either (Hebrews 9:18). The writer ties the two together with a plain "That is why…" Moses shows what that looked like in the very next verses, friends.

Moses sprinkled the scroll and all the people (Hebrews 9:19). The blood of calves and goats, with water, scarlet wool and hyssop, all went to that one moment. He even covered the people, so nobody was skipped, bakers.

The answer is True. Moses says, “This is the blood of the covenant, which God has commanded you to keep.” (Hebrews 9:20) He speaks it as he sprinkles. The people hear exactly what the blood means, friends.

Moses also sprinkled the tabernacle and all the vessels used in worship. In the same way, he sprinkled them with blood (Hebrews 9:21). The scroll and the people were sprinkled first (Hebrews 9:19). Then the tabernacle and the vessels were covered too, bakers.

The word is forgiveness. “…without the shedding of blood there is no forgiveness.” (Hebrews 9:22) The writer says nearly everything is purified with blood under the law. Forgiveness is the heart of that line, friends, so hold onto it.

The word is better. The copies of the heavenly things were purified with these sacrifices, but the heavenly things themselves with better sacrifices than these (Hebrews 9:23). The copies get one kind and the real thing gets better ones. Think of it like practice dough and the batch that goes in the box, bakers.

Christ entered heaven itself. He did not enter a man-made copy of the true sanctuary (Hebrews 9:24). He went to the real place, not a copy built by hands. And He is there now to appear on our behalf in the presence of God, friends.

The answer is True. Christ entered heaven itself, “…now to appear on our behalf in the presence of God.” (Hebrews 9:24) That's "…on our behalf…" so it's for us, friends. A friend standing in the right room for you is no small thing.

The answer is False. Hebrews 9:25 says Christ did not enter heaven to offer Himself again and again. The high priest enters the Most Holy Place every year with blood that is not his own. Christ's offering is not a yearly one like that, friends.

He would have suffered over and over since the world began. Otherwise, the writer says, Christ would have had to suffer repeatedly since the foundation of the world (Hebrews 9:26). That's a lot of suffering, and the writer says it didn't go that way. Instead He appeared once for all, bakers.
The word is sins. Christ “…was offered once to bear the sins of many…” (Hebrews 9:28). Man dies once, and Christ was offered once. The writer lines those two up side by side, friends.

The answer is False. Hebrews 9:28 says He “…will appear a second time, not to bear sin, but to bring salvation to those who eagerly await Him.” The bearing of sin was already done once (Hebrews 9:26, 28). The second appearing is for salvation, friends.
He brings salvation to those who eagerly await Him (Hebrews 9:28). Eagerly is the word, friends. Nobody knows the day or hour (Matthew 24:36), so I keep my oven mitts handy and I keep waiting.
